subject: Control/Data Plane escape-hatch & fault-containment - ops handbook review
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-infra.com>, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control/Data Plane escape-hatch & fault-containment - ops handbook review

Hi team —

Following our run of staging failovers last week I put together a focused ops handbook draft that codifies how we handle plane-level faults (control-plane isolation, data-plane degraded modes, and the operator "escape hatch" when we need to route around a broken dependency). The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incidents and make our rollback/fallback deterministic for customers running the Private VPC package.

What's attached:
- plane-fault-matrix.xlsx (mapping of failure modes to containment actions, severity, SLO impact)
- ops-escape-hatch-runbook-diff.md (delta from our standard staging runbook — highlights the new isolated-controlplane + degraded-replica flow)

High-level asks:
1) Can you validate the containment steps for control-plane partitioning? I called out three options: local control-plane-only mode, regional fallback, and explicit tenant drain.
2) Are observability/alerting thresholds reasonable (column F in the matrix)?
3) Any missing prescriptive rollback commands or K8s job snippets that should be added to the runbook?

I've highlighted a few contested decisions in the sheet: e.g., whether to allow KV-cache warm start during partial data-plane outages (I suggested conservative skip to avoid inconsistent responses).

Please drop comments in the Drive link or reply inline. I want to lock this by Thursday so we can push a trimmed version into the Dedicated onboarding pack.

Thanks,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-infra.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane escape-hatch & fault-containment - ops handbook review

Thanks, Sofia — good timing. Quick notes after a first pass through the matrix:

- For the control-plane-only mode: can we add a step to explicitly rotate inter-node mTLS certs (or at least verify cert expiry) before allowing traffic to resume? We've seen cert skew cause follow-on failures during previous partial restarts.
- The suggested conservative KV-cache skip makes sense for consistency, but it will spike latency for bursty workloads. Can the runbook include a short procedure for manual cache snapshotting so CS can rehydrate a bounded set of prefixes?

I'll push a commented copy to the Drive (devops@acme-infra will also be watching). Tim from our infra team is copied — Tim, can you confirm whether the regional fallback requires any BGP change or if it's handled entirely by our overlay?

Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Operations, Acme Infra
elena.rossi@acme-infra.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-infra.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane escape-hatch & fault-containment - ops handbook review

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 11:03 AM Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-infra.com> wrote:
> For the control-plane-only mode: can we add a step to explicitly rotate inter-node mTLS certs (or at least verify cert expiry) before allowing traffic to resume?

Good call — adding an automated cert-check job makes sense. I've sketched the k8s CronJob in the Drive (under /playbooks/cronjobs) that will check cert TTL and emit a "cert-at-risk" alert. If triggered we won't auto-join nodes back into the control plane until an operator acknowledges.

Regarding the manual cache snapshot — quick note: instead of full snapshotting we could add a lightweight prefix dump API (read-only) that CS can call to rehydrate only high-value prefixes. I've put a sample curl + python helper in the runbook diff (lines ~45-60). That avoids the heavy snapshot/restore path and keeps warm starts safer.

Inline comments in the spreadsheet (column H) also suggest we add a short "traffic classification" appendix so on-call knows which tenants can be routed to degraded replicas without violating data locality contracts.

Action items I'm taking:
- Add CronJob snippet and alert mapping to the runbook (will upload patch).
- Add prefix-dump helper and call example.
- Quick appendix for tenant-classification (requesting Marissa to sketch classification tags).

Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Staff Engineer, Runtime Orchestration | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane escape-hatch & fault-containment - ops handbook review

Thanks — reviewed and looks good to me. A couple of small edits I recommend before locking:

- Make the operator "escape hatch" explicit: add a short checklist (3 bullets) at the top of the runbook with the exact phone/pager escalation order and required sign-offs for a regional fallback.
- Note on SLAs: explicitly call out which customer tiers get automatic degraded-replica routing vs. manual approval. That avoids noisy paging for Standard customers.

If everyone agrees I can schedule a 30-minute readout Thursday at 10:00 PT to finalize and push the trimmed artifacts to the Dedicated onboarding pack.

Kim
